Tension, compression & shear calculator

Axial and shear stress, strain, elongation and stiffness of a prismatic bar.

How it works

Hooke's law for a bar: under axial force it stretches (σ = E·ε), and under transverse force it shears (τ = G·γ). Stiffness depends on the material (E, G) and the shape (A/l).

Key points

  • Axial stiffness C_z = E·A/l. Long, thin members are compliant.
  • G = E/(2(1+ν)) ≈ 0.38·E for metals.
  • The bar also narrows sideways by the Poisson ratio: Δh/h = −ν·ε.
  • Combined stresses are checked with von Mises: σ_V = √(σ² + 3τ²).

Assumptions

  • Uniform stress over the section (average shear)
  • Linear elastic
